hold-up-your-heads-girls-helps-for-girls: Annie Ryder wrote this encouraging guide for girls navigating school, work, and growing up in the early 1900s. Her advice covers study habits, friendships, manners, and keeping one's self-respect in a world with limited opportunities for women. Warm, practical, and earnest, it shows what well-meaning adults wanted young women to hear.
once-upon-a-time-in-connecticut: Caroline Clifford Newton gathers stories of colonial Connecticut for young readers — pioneer days, old customs, and the making of a state. Written to give children a love of their local past, the tales mix history with fireside charm. A delightful introduction to New England heritage.
the-development-of-religious-liberty-in-: M. Louise Greene traces the slow growth of religious liberty in Connecticut — from stern Puritan establishment to full freedom of conscience. Her careful, scholarly history lights up a hard-won American right. An important and thorough state study. Her thorough research gives the story its full and proper weight.
